sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing in a neutral pose. Panel 2: full-body true side profile. Panel 3: full-body back view showing the back of the coat and the back of the wig. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera, neutral expression, face clearly lit. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the wig to the tips of the webbed toes with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels. Layout detail: the sheet looks like four photographs mounted side by side on one horizontal board, divided from left to right by three vertical gaps into four tall narrow panels, each a separate photo of the same frog; never paint it as one single continuous picture.

Subject: the Frog-Footman, a male, a photoreal CGI common frog (Rana temporaria) scaled up to dream size, about 80 cm tall when standing, a heavy adult frog with a real frog body and not a human frame. In the three full-body panels he stands up on his hind legs the way a frog rises for a bow, in a frog's semi-crouch: thick frog thighs and long shanks bent at the knee and splayed outward, never straight human legs; squat, soft, pear-shaped body, widest at the belly, with the flat head sitting directly on the body and no neck at all; short frog forelimbs with four frog fingers ending in round toe tips; bare webbed hind feet with long toes. Round, broad, flat frog head with a very wide mouth line; very large round bulging eyes set right at the top of the head, gold-bronze irises with horizontal black pupils, gazing vacantly upward; moist skin, olive-brown mottled with darker blotches, a dark mask patch behind each eye, pale cream-yellow throat and belly. Placid, vacant expression, throat softly pulsing. Wearing: a faded 1862 household footman's livery cut for a frog-bodied footman: a snuff-brown wool tail coat worn thin and much-brushed at the cuffs with plain tarnished brass buttons and no crest or badge, a plain buff wool waistcoat, cream knee breeches, and a slightly dishevelled powdered white wig of tight sausage curls set on the frog's head; the webbed hands, lower legs and webbed feet left in natural moist frog skin; rumpled from sitting on the ground. The powdered wig sits on top of the frog head and does not replace it; the frog skin runs continuously into the collar so the head never reads as a mask. Naturalistic amphibian anatomy with real moist speckled skin and soft specular highlights; not a person in costume.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.

Layout recap (highest priority): four separate panels side by side, exactly one frog in each panel, front / side / back full-body views and one head-and-shoulders close-up of the same frog.
